units: pixels (x right, y down, origin top-left of the 1920x1080 frame) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.motion: static (water background mean abs difference between frame 0 and frames 1..40 < 2 grey levels in object-free regions; seabed outline identical in all frames)
camera.focal_length: unknown - estimate from given depths + a known size (see notes.md)
camera.perspective_cues: No horizon visible (open blue water). Seabed dunes occupy the bottom ~12% of the image (crest line y~915-975 px, x 0-1400; darker far seabed at right, y>1050). Sun rays (god rays) fan down from the top centre (x~900-1100). Camera looks roughly horizontally / slightly upward toward the surface.

apparent_size_change.shark: grows strongly: body-core height (fins removed) 154 px at f0 -> 175 px f20 -> 263 px f36 -> 319 px f40 (factor ~2.07 f0->f40); full mask length (fully visible frames) 554 px f20 -> 858 px f36 -> 901 px f37. The shark comes closer to the camera while swimming right-to-left.
apparent_size_change.turtle: roughly constant: body-core height 98 px f0, 115 px f20, 113 px f36, 115 px f40 (varies +-15% with flipper strokes); shell top y stays at 645-658 px. Turtle stays at roughly constant depth; may approach slightly (~10-15%).

objects.name: shark
objects.description: great white shark, large grey-blue body with white belly, dorsal fin and crescent tail; the upper animal (y ~0-430 px)
objects.cut_by_frame_edge: frames 0-19 tail beyond right edge (x=1919); frames 38-40 snout beyond left edge (x=0) and at f40 dorsal fin at top edge
objects.heading: swims right-to-left (snout to the left), slightly upward in the image, toward the camera
objects.reference_point: mask centroid (cx,cy) and body-core centroid (core_cx,core_cy; fins/tail removed by morphological opening) - proxy for the rig origin, which is not visible

objects.name: turtle
objects.description: sea turtle (blue-grey shell, long front flippers), the lower animal (y ~645-875 px), smaller on screen
objects.heading: swims right-to-left (head/front flippers to the left), nearly horizontal, flapping front flippers
objects.reference_point: mask centroid and body-core centroid (shell/body after removing flippers; steadier than the full-mask centroid)

objects.name: seabed
objects.description: sandy seabed dunes along the bottom of the frame with animated light caustics (bright cyan patches near x~950-1070,y~930-1000 and x~200-350,y~940)

objects.name: light_rays
objects.description: sun rays / god rays from the surface, vertical bright bands, flicker slightly; not objects

events.event: both animals already swimming leftward; shark image motion very slow at start (~1-2 px/frame) and accelerates monotonically
shark tail fully enters image (shark fully visible f20-f37)
turtle flippers at lowest point (bbox bottom y~873 px, f21-f24); upstroke afterwards
shark snout reaches left image edge (x=0); shark starts leaving image
last frame; shark dorsal fin touches top edge; turtle flippers back near horizontal

no_contacts: the shark and turtle never touch or overlap in the image (shark always above y~430, turtle below y~640)
